result.keywords: This article explores a hybrid smart-material platform that merges resistive memory arrays with thermally driven phase-transition actuation to support compact in-sensor and in-memory computation. By combining programmable soft chambers with RRAM-like switching elements, the system enables remote, low-power control of deformation while performing vector-matrix operations at the device level. The work discusses device physics, peripheral circuitry, and system integration for autonomous robotics and edge neural accelerators, emphasizing dense integration, ultra-low energy operation, and scalable architectures for adaptive sensing, actuation, and computation.
result.title: Resilient Phase-Transition Memory Actuators for In-Situ Neural Computation.
